q: What property makes binary search on the answer valid?
options: Feasibility is monotonic: once an answer works, all bigger ones work
why: The yes/no answers form no…no yes…yes, so there is one boundary to find.

q: For Koko Eating Bananas, why is hi = max(piles)?
options: At that speed every pile takes one hour; faster never helps
why: Eating faster than the largest pile can't reduce any pile below one hour.

q: For Ship Packages Within D Days, why is lo = max(weights) and not 1?
options: A capacity smaller than the heaviest package can never ship it
why: Packages can't be split, so any capacity below the heaviest one is infeasible.

q: Checking feasibility is O(n) and the answer range is up to 10⁹. Total cost?
why: Binary search over 10⁹ values needs about 30 steps.

q: Hours for a pile of 7 bananas at speed 3, using (p + k − 1) // k?
Which phrase most strongly suggests binary search on the answer?
why: Minimize-the-maximum / maximize-the-minimum with an easy check is the classic signal.
